newsitem.title: SPAIN: S&P ups city of Barcelona rating to "AA-"from "A".
newsitem.headline: S&P ups city of Barcelona rating to "AA-"from "A".

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had lifted its long term debt ratings for the city of Barcelona to "AA-" from "A".
In a statement S&P's said Barcelona's outlook was rated stable.

S&P said the upgrade was based on an overall improvement of the city's financial performance, "which has allowed it to fully finance its investments and to reduce absolute debt levels for the second consecutive year".
"In 1996 the city government showed a healthy operating surplus of 18 percent of operating revenues that allowed the city to full self finance its capital program," the statement added.

"Due to large fiscal imbalances in the late 1980s and early 1990s the city's current debt level at 134 percent of operating revenues (down from 150 percent in 1995) remains somewhat high by national strandards, although it is similar to some subnational entities in other countries that carry the same rating" S&P said.
"The government fiscal targets contemplate further reduction of this ratio to below 100 percent by the end of the decade...Recent accomplishments are encouraging," it added.
